key_facts: Creative Bloq columnist Tom May writes that Elon Musk objected to the term 'slopcore' for AI music, saying it is really 'awesomecore'.
The column links this to President Trump's attempt to rebrand 'artificial intelligence' as 'super intelligence', with Trump declaring on Truth Social that those who still say it are 'THE ENEMY'.
May argues renaming usually signals a toxic brand and compares it to prunes becoming 'dried plums' and Royal Mail's brief 'Consignia'.
He cites a Gallup survey finding 70% of Americans oppose data centres in their communities.
He cites Data Center Watch: about 45 data centre projects worth $68 billion were blocked or delayed between April and June.
quote_evidence: "Calling it slopcore is a misnomer," he said. "Frankly, it's awesomecore."
"A good brand is what people say about you when you're not in the room."
why_it_matters_hint: An opinion column reading the rebranding as a sign AI boosters fear public opinion.
event_date: Musk remark 'a few days ago'; column published 15 Oct 2026
notes: Opinion column, analysis is the author's view.
title: Elon Musk's attempts to rebrand AI slop are hilarious, but they betray a deeper truth
